Summary of the  Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
Key Provisions 
1.	Applicability
•	Extends to the whole of India.
•	Applies to branches/offices/agencies outside India owned/controlled by persons resident in India.
•	Applies to contraventions outside India by persons to whom the Act applies.
2.	Regulation and Management of Foreign Exchange
•	Section 3: Prohibits dealing in foreign exchange with non-authorised persons, certain payments, and financial transactions for acquiring assets outside India without permission.
•	Section 4: Restricts holding of foreign exchange, foreign securities, or immovable property outside India by persons resident in India.
•	Section 5: Allows current account transactions with authorised persons, subject to reasonable restrictions by the Central Government.
•	Section 6: Regulates capital account transactions, with the Reserve Bank specifying permissible transactions, limits, and conditions.
•	Section 7: Mandates declaration and realisation of export proceeds.
•	Section 8: Requires realisation and repatriation of foreign exchange due to persons in India.
•	Section 9: Exempts certain cases from realisation and repatriation requirements.
3.	Authorised Person
•	Sections 10-12: Define authorised persons, Reserve Bank's powers to issue directions, inspect, and more.
4.	Contraventions and Penalties
•	Sections 13-15: Outline penalties, enforcement, and power to compound contraventions.
5.	Adjudication and Appeal
•	Sections 16-19: Establish the Adjudicating Authority, appeal processes to the Special Director (Appeals), and the Appellate Tribunal.
